0.zh: 第一部分 法权学说

en: Right must be considered 1. in itself and 2. in its existence in the state society.
zh: 必须 1. 就权利本身、2. 就它在国家社会中的存在加以考察。

en: According to right only the general will is to come about, without regard to the intention or conviction of the individual, and right has man for its object only as a free being as such.
zh: 按照权利，只有普遍意志应当实现，而不考虑个别者的意图或确信；权利只把人作为自由的存在者本身当作自己的对象。

en: Right consists in this: that every individual be respected and treated by the other as a free being, for only in that way does the free will have itself in the other for its object and content.
zh: 权利在于：每一个个别者都被他人当作自由的存在者而尊重和对待；因为唯有就此而言，自由意志才在他人之中以自己为对象和内容。

en: Explanation.
The freedom of the individual underlies right, and right consists in this: that I treat the other as a free being.
Reason demands a juridical form of conduct.
In respect of its essence everyone is a freeman.
Men are distinguished by their particular states and characteristics, but this distinction concerns the abstract will as such in no way.
In this they are the same, and in respecting the other one respects oneself.
It follows from this that through the violation of one individual’s right all are violated in their right.
This is a quite different kind of participation than merely sharing in another’s damage.

For 1. the damage or loss which someone suffers in respect of goods of fortune — whose good state is indeed desirable but is not necessary in itself — does concern me; yet I cannot say that it simply ought not to have happened at all; 2. such states belong to the particularity of man.
Despite all participation we separate misfortunes from ourselves and regard them as something alien.
By contrast, when the right of another is injured, everyone feels himself immediately touched, because right is something universal.
A violation of right therefore cannot be regarded by us as something alien.
We are harder injured by it, because right is necessary.
zh: 诠释。
权利以个别者的自由为基础，而权利在于：我把他人当作自由的存在者来对待。
理性要求一种法权上的行为。
就其本质而言，每个人都是一个自由者。
人们因各自特殊的状态与特性而彼此不同，但这种差别与作为这样的抽象意志毫不相干。
在这一点上他们是同一个东西；而且人们尊重他人时，也就是在尊重自己。
由此可知：一个人权利受到侵犯，所有人的权利也都受到了侵犯。
这是一种与仅仅对他人损失表示关切完全不同的关切。
因为 1. 一个人在祸福之物上遭受的损害或损失——这些祸福之物的良好状态虽是值得愿望的，但自在自为地并不是必然的——固然也与我有关，但我不能说它压根就不该发生；2. 这类状态属于人的特殊性。
尽管有这样的关切，我们仍把不幸事件与自己分开，并把它们看作外在的东西。
相反，当他人权利受到侵害时，每个人都感到自己直接被触及，因为权利是某种普遍的东西。
所以，侵犯权利这件事我们不能看作外在的东西。
由于权利是必然的，我们由此受到的侵害更为沉重。

en: Insofar as everyone is recognised as a free being, he is a person.
The proposition of right can therefore also be expressed thus: everyone shall be treated by the other as a person.
zh: 就每个人被承认为自由的存在者而言，他就是一个人格。
因此，权利命题也可以这样表述：每个人都应当被他人当作人格来对待。

en: Explanation.
The concept of personality includes in itself the I-hood or individuality, which is a free or universal something.
Men have personality through their spiritual nature.
zh: 诠释。
人格性的概念本身包含着我性或个别性，而这种我性或个别性是自由的、普遍者。
人们凭借其精神本性而具有人格性。

en: It follows from this that no man can be compelled to anything except only to annul the compulsion which he has done to others.
zh: 由此可知：没有人能被强制去做别的事，只能是去撤销他施加于他人的强制。

en: Explanation.
There are limitations of freedom and laws which allow that men be treated not as persons but as things, e.g. the laws which permit slavery.
But these are only positive laws, rights, and indeed laws which are opposed to reason or to absolute right.
zh: 诠释。
有一些对自由的限制和法律，它们容许人们不被当作人格、而是被当作物来对待，例如允许奴隶制的那些法律。
但这些不过是实定法、法，而且是那些与理性或与绝对权利相对立的实定法、法。

en: That action which limits the freedom of another, or does not recognise and allow him to count as a free will, is contrary to right.
zh: 那种限制他人自由、或不把他人承认为并视作自由意志的行为，是不合于法的。

en: Explanation.

In the absolute sense compulsion against man is properly impossible, because everyone is a free being, because he can assert his will against necessity and can give up everything which belongs to his determinate being.
Compulsion occurs in the following way.
To one side of man’s determinate being something is appended as a condition of the same, so that if he wants to preserve the former, he must also put up with the other.
Because man’s determinate being is dependent on external objects, he can be seized on one side of his determinate being.
Man is compelled only when he wants something with which something else is still connected, and it depends on his will whether he wants the one and thereby also the other, or neither of the two.
Insofar as he is compelled after all, that to which he is determined is also contained in his will.
Compulsion is in that respect only something relative.
It is juridical when it is exercised in order to assert right against the individual.
This compulsion has one side on which it is no compulsion and does not contradict the dignity of a free being, because the will in and for itself is also the absolute will of everyone.
Freedom in general is present where the law, and not the arbitrariness of an individual, rules.
zh: 诠释。
在绝对的意义上，对人的强制其实是不可能的，因为每个人都是自由的存在者，因为他能够坚持自己的意志以对抗必然性，并且能够放弃一切属于他定在的东西。
强制是以下述方式发生的。
在人的定在的某一侧，会把某个东西作为它的条件联结上去；这样一来，如果他要保住前者，就也必须忍受后者。
因为人的定在依赖外在的对象，所以他可能在定在的某一侧被抓住。
只有当人想要某个东西、而这东西还与另一样东西相联结时，他才会被强制；而他是否想要这一个、从而也想要那一个，或者两者都不想要，则取决于他的意志。
就他终究还是被强制而言，他被规定去做的那个东西，也还是蕴含在他的意志之中。
就此而言，强制不过是某种相对的东西。
当它被行使、以便针对个别人主张权利时，它就是合于法的。
这种强制有一个方面，就这一方面而言它并不是强制，也不违背自由存在者的尊严，因为意志自在自为地也是每个人的绝对意志。
自由总归发生在法律而非某个个别者的任意占统治地位的地方。

en: Everything which does not limit the freedom of others or annul any act of theirs is allowed — but not thereby commanded — in law.
zh: 凡是不限制他人自由、也不取消其任何自由行为的，在法上都是允许的，但并不因此就是被命令的。

en: Explanation.
Right properly contains only prohibitions, no commands, and what is not prohibited is allowed.
It is true, however, that one can express the prohibitions of right positively as commands, e.g. "you shall keep the contract!".
The general principle of right, of which the others are only particular applications, is: "you shall leave the property of another uninjured!".
This does not mean: you shall render something positive to the other or bring about a change in circumstances, but contains only the refraining from violation of property.
If, then, right is expressed as a positive command, this is only a form of expression under which, as to content, a prohibition always lies.
zh: 诠释。
法其实只包含禁令，不包含命令；没有被禁止的，就是被允许的。
不过人们可以把法的禁令正面表述为命令，例如「你应当履行契约！」
那个一般法原则——其他一切法都只是它的特殊应用——就是：「你应当不损害他人的财产！」
这不是说：你应当为他人做某种正面的事，或者促成某种情形的变化，而只是包含着不去侵犯财产。
所以，当法被表述为正面的命令时，这不过是一种表述形式，就内容而言其底下始终是禁令。

en: The will, in that it subsumes a thing under itself, makes it its own.
Possession is this being-subsumed-ness of a thing under my will.
zh: 意志把一个物归摄于自己之下，从而使它成为自己的东西。
占有就是这样一个物被归摄于我的意志之下。

en: Explanation.
Subsumption comprises two things: something universal and something individual.
I subsume something individual when I lay upon it a universal determinacy.
This subsumption occurs above all in judging.
The subsuming in judging is the predicate and the subsumed the subject.
Taking possession is the expression of the judgment that a thing becomes mine.
My will is here the subsuming.
I give the thing the predicate of being mine.
The will is the subsuming for all external things, because it is the universal essence in itself.
All things, however, which do not themselves refer to themselves, are only necessary, not free.
This relation thus makes it so that man has the right to take all external things into possession and to make out of them something other than what they themselves are.
He treats them thus only in accordance with their essence.
zh: 诠释。
归摄包含两个方面：某个普遍者与某个个别者。
当我给某个个别者加上一项普遍的规定时，我就在归摄这个个别者。
这种归摄总归出现在判断之中。
判断中的归摄者是谓词，被归摄者是主体。
占有取得就是说出这样一个判断：一个物成为我的东西。
在这里，我的意志就是归摄者。
我给这个物以「是我的东西」这个谓词。
意志是所有外在物的归摄者，因为它自在自为地就是普遍的本质。
但一切不是以自身为自身之根据的物，都只是必然的，而不是自由的。
所以这一关系使人有权把所有外在物占有下来，并把它们做成一个不同于它们自身的东西。
他这样对待它们，只是与它们的本质相合。

en: The thing which is first to be taken into possession must 1. be res nullius, i.e. not yet subsumed under another will.
zh: 那首先要去占有的物必须是 1. res nullius，也就是说，还没有归摄于另一个意志之下。

en: Explanation.
A thing which is already another’s I may not take into possession — not because it is a thing, but because it is his thing.
For if I take the thing into possession, I annul on it the predicate of being his and thereby negate his will.
The will is something absolute which I cannot make into something negative.
zh: 诠释。
一个已经属于他人的物，我不能拿去占有；这不是因为它是一个物，而是因为它是他的物。
因为如果我把那个物占有下来，我就在它身上扬弃了「是他的东西」这个谓词，从而否定他的意志。
意志是某种绝对的东西，我不能把它做成某个否定的东西。

en: Possession must be seized, i.e. it must be made recognisable to the others that I want to have subsumed this object under my will — whether by bodily seizing, by forming, or at least by designating the object.
zh: 占有必须被抓住，也就是说，必须让他人看出我要把这个对象归摄于我的意志之下：或通过身体的抓取，或通过塑形，或至少通过对对象的标记。

en: Explanation.
The inner act of will must precede the external seizing of possession; it expresses that the thing is to be mine.
The first kind of taking possession is bodily seizing.

It has the defect that the objects to be seized must be so constituted that I can grasp them immediately with the hand or cover them with my body; and further that it is not lasting. - The second, more perfect kind is forming, that I give a thing a shape, e.g. cultivate a field, make gold into a cup.
Here the form of what is mine is immediately connected with the object and is therefore in and for itself a sign that the matter too belongs to me.
Forming belongs to, among other things, the planting of trees, the taming and feeding of animals.

An imperfect kind of land possession is the use of a district without forming it, e.g. when nomadic peoples use a territory for pasture, hunting peoples for the hunt, fishing peoples the shore of a sea or river.

Such a taking of possession is still superficial, because the actual use is only for the first time a temporary way, not yet one that lasts and adheres to the object. - Taking possession by mere designation of the object is imperfect.

The sign which, unlike in forming, does not at the same time constitute the thing itself is a thing which has a meaning, but that meaning is not its own essence and it therefore behaves towards it as something alien.
But it also otherwise has a meaning of its own which does not cohere with the nature of the thing designated through it.
Designation is therefore arbitrary.
What a thing is to be a sign of is more or less a matter of convenience.
zh: 诠释。
外在的占有抓取之前，必须有内在的意志行为，它表明这个物应当是我的。
占有取得的第一种方式是身体的抓取。
它有这样一个缺陷：待抓取的对象必须是这样的——我能够直接用手抓住它或用我的身体遮住它；此外它还并不是持久的。——第二种、更完满的方式是塑形，即我给一个东西以形状，例如耕种一块田、把黄金做成一只杯子。
在这里，「我的东西」这一形式与对象直接联结，因而自在自为地就是一个符号，表明连物质也属于我。
塑形还包括别的东西，例如栽种树木、驯养和喂养动物。
一种不完满的土地占有方式，是在不塑形的情况下使用一个地区；例如游牧民族为放牧而使用一片地带，狩猎民族为打猎而使用它，捕鱼民族使用一片海岸或一条河。
这样的占有取得还是表面的，因为真正的使用只是一种暂时的、还没有持久地附着在对象上的方式。——仅通过对对象的标记而占有取得是不完满的。
这个符号不像塑形中那样同时构成物本身，它是一个具有某种意义的东西，但那意义并不是它自己的本质；因此这个符号相对于它就是一个外在者。
不过它也有别的属于它自己的意义，而这意义并不与它所标记之物的本性本身相联系。
所以标记是任意的。
一个物应当成为什么的符号，多或少是权宜之事。

en: Posssession becomes property, or becomes so juridically, insofar as it is acknowledged by all others that the thing which I have made my own is mine, just as I equally acknowledge the possession of others as theirs.

My possession is acknowledged because it is an act of the free will, which is something absolute in itself and in which the universal lies, that I likewise regard the willing of others as something absolute.
zh: 占有就成为财产，或者说在法上就是如此：就所有人都承认那个我已变成自己东西的物是我的而言，正如我也承认他人的占有是他们的。
我的占有之所以得到承认，是因为它是自由意志的一个行为，而这个行为自身包含着某种绝对的东西；普遍者就蕴藏在其中——我把别人的意愿同样看作某个绝对的东西。

en: Explanation.
Possession and property are two different determinacies.
It is not necessary that possession and property should always be connected.
It is possible that I have a property without being in possession of it.
If, for example, I lend something to another, it always remains my property, even though I do not possess it.
Possession and property are contained in the concept that I have a dominium over something.
Property is the juridical side of the dominium, and possession is only the external side, that something is as such in my power.
The juridical is the side of my absolute free will, which has declared something to be its own.
This will must be acknowledged by others, because it is in and for itself and insofar as the previously stated conditions have been observed. - Property thus has an inner and an outer side.
The former in itself is the taking of possession, the latter the act of the will, which as such must be acknowledged.
It seems contingent or arbitrary whether the acknowledgement of others also supervenes upon a taking of possession.
But it must supervene, because it lies in the nature of the thing.
Acknowledging has not its ground in mutuality.
I do not acknowledge it on the ground that you acknowledge it and conversely; rather, the ground of this mutual acknowledgement is the nature of the thing itself.
I acknowledge the will of the other because it is in and for itself to be acknowledged.
zh: 诠释。
占有与财产是两个不同的规定。
占有与财产并不必然总是联结在一起。
我可能拥有一项财产而并不占有它。
例如当我借给别人某物时，它始终是我的财产，尽管我并不占有它。
占有与财产都包含在这样一个概念里：我对某物有一种支配权。
财产是支配权的法权方面，而占有只是那个外在的方面：某物总归处在我的权力之中。
法权的方面是我绝对自由意志的那一面，这个意志已把某物宣布为自己的东西。
这个意志必须得到他人的承认，因为它自在自为地如此，并且就此而言前面所说的条件已被遵守。——所以财产有一个内在的方面和一个外在的方面。
前者就其自身而言是占有取得，后者则是那个必须被承认为这样的意志行为。
在一场占有取得中他人的承认是否也随之而来，似乎是偶然的或任意的。
但它必须随之而来，因为这是由物的本性所决定的。
承认并不是以相互性为根据的。
我承认，并不是因为你承认它、并且反之亦然；这一相互承认的根据正是物本身的本性。
我承认他人的意志，因为他自在自为地就是应当被承认的。

en: I can divest myself of my property, and the same can pass to others through my free will.
zh: 我可以舍弃我的财产，而同一项财产可以通过我的自由意志转移给他人。

en: Explanation.
My powers and skills are indeed my own most proper property, but they too have an externality.
According to the abstract determinacy they are already external insofar as I can distinguish them from me, the simple I.
But even in itself the powers and skills are individual and limited, and do not constitute my essence itself.
My essence, which is universal in itself, is distinguished from these particular determinacies.
Finally they are external in their use.
Precisely by using them I make them into an external form, and what is brought forth through them is some external determinate being.
In the use the power as such does not lie, but it preserves itself, notwithstanding that it has expressed itself and made this expression of its own into a determinate being different from it.

This expression of the power is also something external insofar as it is something limited and finite. - Insofar as something is my property, I have indeed connected it with my will, but this connection is not an absolute one; for were it such, my would have to lie in this thing in respect of its essence.
Rather, I have made my will here into something particular only, and can, because it is free, annul this particularity again.
zh: 诠释。
我的力量与技能固然是我最本己的财产，但它们也有一个外在方面。
按照抽象的规定，它们就已经就此而言是外在的，即我能把它们与我自己、这个单纯的自我区分开。
但即使自在自为地，这些力量与技能也是个别而受限制的，并不构成我的本质本身。
我的本质，即那自在自为地是普遍者的东西，与这些特殊规定相区别。
最后，它们在使用中是外在的。
恰恰在我使用它们时，我把它们做成一种外在的形式，而通过它们产生出来的东西是某种外在的定在。
在使用中所涉及的并不是作为这样的力量，而是力量自身得以保持，尽管它表现了自己并把自己的这种表现做成了一个不同于它的定在。
力量的这种表现同样就此而言是某种外在的东西，因为它是某个受限制而有限的东西。——就某物是我的财产而言，我固然已把我的意志与它联结起来，但这一联结不是绝对的；因为如果它是绝对的话，我的意志就其本质而言必须在这物之中。
我只是在这里把我的意志做成了某个特殊的东西；而且因为它是自由的，我又能取消这一特殊性。

en: Those goods are inalienable which are not so much my possession or property as constitute my most own person or are contained in my essence, such as the freedom of the will, ethical life, religion, and so forth.
zh: 凡并非更多属于我的占有或财产，而毋宁构成我的最属我的人格、或包含在我的本质之中的那些物，都是不可让渡的，如意志的自由、伦理、宗教等等。

en: Explanation.
Only those goods are alienable which are already external by their nature.
For instance, I cannot regard personality as something external to me, for insofar as a man has given up his personality, he has made himself into a thing.

But such an alienation would be null and void. - One would alienate one’s ethical life if, for instance, one made oneself responsible to another to perform at his command all manner of actions, crimes as well as indifferent actions.
Such an obligation would have no force, because it includes within itself the freedom of the will, in which each must stand for himself.
Ethical or unethical deeds are the own actions of the one who performs them, and since they are of such a kind, I cannot alienate them. - Nor can I alienate my religion.
If a community or even an individual had left it to a third person to determine what their faith ought to consist in, this would be an obligation which anyone could unilaterally lift.
No wrong is done to the other person with whom I have entered into this obligation, because that which I have left to him could never become his property.
zh: 诠释。
只有那些依其本性已经是外在的物才是可让渡的。
例如，我不能把人格性看作某种对我而言是外在的东西，因为一个人一旦放弃了自己的人格性，他就把自身变成了物。
但这样的让渡将是徒然无效的。——例如，一个人若向另一个人保证，听从他的命令去做出各种各样的行为，罪行也好，无关紧要的行为也好，他就是在让渡自己的伦理。
这样的义务不会有任何效力，因为它把意志的自由包含在自身之中，而在这种自由中，每个人都必须为自己而独立。
伦理的或不合伦理的行为都是实施它们者自己的行为，正因其如此，我不能让渡它们。——我的宗教同样不能让我渡出去。
如果一个教会团体乃至一个个人把它托付给第三者去规定何者应当构成他们的信仰，那将是一项任何一方都可以单方面扬弃的义务。
我与之订立了这项义务的另一方并不因此受到不义对待，因为我让给他的东西从来不可能成为他的财产。

en: By contrast, I can alienate the determinate use of my spiritual and physical powers and the thing which I hold in possession.
zh: 与此相反，我可以把我精神和身体之力的特定使用，以及我所占有的物让渡出去。

en: Explanation.
One can alienate only a limited use of one’s powers, because this use or the limited effect is distinguished from the power.
But the constant use or the effect in its entire scope cannot be distinguished from the power in itself.
The power is the inner or the universal as against its expression.
The expressions are a determinate being limited in space and time.
The power in itself is not exhausted in any single such determinate being, nor is it bound to any one of its contingent effects.
But secondly, the power must operate and express itself, otherwise it is no power.

Thirdly, the whole scope of its effects constitutes the power itself, for the whole scope of expression is itself again the universal which the power is, and for that reason man cannot alienate the entire use of his powers; otherwise he would alienate his personality.
zh: 诠释。
人只能让渡其力的受限制的使用，因为这种使用或这种受限制的效果是同力本身相区分的。
但恒常的使用或整个范围内的效果，则不能同自在的力相区分。
力即是相对于其表现而言的内在者或普遍者。
这些表现是一个在空间和时间中受限制的定在。
自在的力并不在任何单个这样的定在中耗尽，也不系于其任何一种偶然的效果。
但其次，力必须起作用并把自己表现出来，否则它就不是力。
第三，一切效果的全部范围本身即构成力，因为表现的全部范围又正是力所是的那普遍者；因此人不能让自己之力的全部使用让渡出去，否则他就把自身的人格性让渡出去了。

en: An alienation to another requires my consent to leave the thing to him, and his consent to accept it.
This double consent, insofar as it is mutually declared and uttered as valid, is called a contract (pactum).
zh: 向他者作出的让渡，须有我同意把物交给他，也须有他同意接受它。
这种双重的同意，只要它被相互宣告并被宣示为有效，就叫做契约（pactum）。

en: Explanation.
The contract is a particular way in which one becomes owner of a thing which already belongs to another.
The way of becoming owner set out earlier was the immediate taking possession of a thing which was res nullius.
As the simplest kind of contract one may take the contract of gift, in which one person simply leaves a thing to another without receiving compensation for its value.

A valid gift is a contract, because the will of both must be present, of the one who, without taking anything back in return, leaves the thing to the other, and of the other who accepts the thing. - 2.
The contract of exchange consists in my leaving something of my property to another on the condition that he give me a thing of equal value in return.
This requires the double consent of each: to give something away and to accept what is offered by the other in return. - 3.
Buying and selling is a particular kind of exchange, of goods against money.
Money is the universal commodity, which therefore, as the abstract value, cannot itself be used to satisfy any particular need.
It is only the universal means of obtaining the particular needs.
The use of money is only an indirect one.
A matter is not money in and for itself, as having these qualities, but one only lets it count as such by convention. - 4.
The lease consists in my leaving to someone my possession or the use of my property, while reserving the property itself for myself.

It may happen here that the person to whom I have lent something must give me back exactly the same thing, or that I have reserved my property for myself in a thing of the same kind or of the same value.
zh: 诠释。
契约是一个人成为某物之所有者的特殊方式，而这个物已经属于另一个人。
先前阐明的那种成为所有者的方式，是对一件 res nullius 的直接占有取得。
契约最简单的一种可以认为是赠与契约，其中只是一个人把物让与另一个人，而不取得对其价值的补偿。
有效的赠与是一项契约，因为双方的意志都必须在场：一方不取回任何回报而把物让与另一方，另一方则接受该物。——2.
交换契约在于：我以他给我一件价值相等的物作为条件，把我的财产中的某物让与另一个人。
这需要每一方的双重同意：让出某物，并接受对方所给予的物作为回报。——3.
购买和出售是交换的一种特殊形式，即以商品换取金钱。
金钱是普遍的商品，因而作为抽象的价值，它本身不能被用来满足任何特殊的需要。
它不过是用来获取这些特殊需要的普遍手段。
金钱的使用只是间接的使用。
一种物质并不是自在自为地、由于具有这些质而成为金钱，人们只是通过约定让它作此认定。——4.
租赁在于：我把我的占有或我之财产的使用让与某人，但为自己保留财产本身。
这里可能出现这样的情况：我借给东西的那个人必须把完全相同的物还给我；或者，我为自己所保留的财产，是一件同一种类或同一价值的东西。

en: The declaration of will contained in the contract is not yet the realization and execution of the transfer of my thing or work to the other.
This transition on the ground of the contract is the performance
zh: 契约中所包含的意思表示，尚不是我的物或我的劳作转移给对方的现实化与执行。
这种以契约为根据的转移就是给付

en: Explanation.

My promise in the contract contains that I have excluded something through my will from the sphere of what is mine, and at the same time I have acknowledged that the other has taken it into his own sphere.
Since now that something is mine, so far as it depends on me, has its ground in my will, the thing has already through the contract become the property of the other.
Insofar, therefore, as I did not perform what was determined in the contract for the other, or did not put him in possession of it, I would violate his property.
I am therefore obliged by the contract itself to observe it (acquisition by testament).
zh: 诠释。
我在契约中的承诺包含着：我已通过我的意志把某物排除在我的所有领域之外；与此同时，我也承认对方已把它接纳到他的领域之中。
既然某物属于我——就其取决于我而言——是以我的意志为根据的，那么通过契约，该物就已经成为对方的财产。
因此，就我不向对方履行契约所定之事、或者不使对方取得占有而言，我就会侵害他的财产。
因此，我本身就受契约约束而须遵守它（通过遗嘱的取得）。

en: An interference by another into the sphere of my freedom can be either 1.
Of such a kind that he has my property as his own in his possession, or claims it, in the sense that he has the right to it and, if not he but I had the right to it, he would leave it to me.
In this he respects the right as such and merely asserts that in this particular case it is on his side.
Or else 2. it lies in his action that he does not acknowledge my will at all, and thus violates right as right.
zh: 他人对我的自由领域所作的干预，或者 1.
是这样一种干预：他把我之财产当作自己的东西而占有，或者主张对它的权利——其意味是：他有此权利，而若此权利不属于他而属于我，他就会让给我。
在这件事上他尊重权利本身，只是主张在这个具体情形中该权利在他这一边。
但也可以是 2.：他的行为根本不承认我的意志，因而把权利作为权利加以侵害。

en: Explanation.
The concepts so far considered contain the nature of right, its laws, its necessity.
But right is not such a necessity as the necessity of physical nature, - e.g. the sun cannot leave its orbit.
A flower must be entirely in accordance with its nature.
If, for instance, it does not fulfil its formation, this comes from external influence, not from itself.
Spirit, on the contrary, can, because of its freedom, act against the laws.
It can therefore be acted against right.
Here one must distinguish 1. the universal right, right qua right, 2. the particular right, in so far as it relates merely to the right of a single person to a single thing.
The universal right is that everyone, independently of this property, is at all a legal person.
The interference with right can therefore be such that it merely asserts that this particular right, this particular thing, does not belong to one.
But in doing so the universal right is not violated.
One behaves in this towards one’s opponent as a legal person.

Such a judgment can altogether be considered as a merely negative one, in which what is particular is negated in the predicate; e.g. if I judge: “this stove is not green”, I negate only the predicate of being so and so coloured, not the universal. - In the second case of interference with the right of another, I assert not only that a particular thing is not the property of another, but I also negate that he is a legal person.
I do not treat him as a person.
I make no claim to anything on the ground that I have or believe myself to have the right to it.
I violate right qua right.
Such a judgment belongs to those which are called infinite.
The infinite judgment negates not only the particular from the predicate but also the universal; e.g. “this stove is not a whale” or “it is not memory”.
Since not only the determinate but also the universal of the predicate is negated, nothing is left to the subject.
Such judgments are therefore nonsensical, yet nevertheless correct.
In the same way the violation of right qua right is something possible, which also occurs, but something nonsensical, self-contradictory.
The cases of the first kind belong to civil law, those of the second to criminal law.
The first is also called civil law, the second criminal law.
zh: 诠释。
迄今为止的概念包含着权利的本性、它的规律和它的必然性。
但权利并不是像物理自然的必然性那样的必然之物——例如，太阳不能偏离自己的轨道。
一朵花必须完全依其本性而存在。
例如，如果它没有完成自身的形态，那是由外在的作用造成的，而不是出自它自身。
精神则相反，由于其自由，可以违反规律而行动。
所以人们可以对权利加以违反。
这里必须区分：1. 一般权利，即作为权利的权利；2. 特殊权利，即仅仅涉及单一个人格对某一件物的权利。
一般权利就是：每一个人，无关于这一财产，本身就是一个法律人格。
所以对权利的干预可能是这样一种情形：它只是主张这一特殊权利、这一特殊之物并不属于某人。
但这样做并没有侵害一般权利。
人在其中对待自己的对手，是作为一个法律人格而对待的。
这样的判断总起来可以看作一个单纯的否定判断，其中谓词里的特殊者被否定；例如，如果我判断：「这个炉子不是绿色的」，那么我所否定的只是那种如此这般的着色这一谓词，而不是普遍者。——在对他人权利的第二种干预中，我不仅主张某件特殊之物不是另一人的财产，而且我还否定他是一个法律人格。
我不把他当作人格来对待。
我并非根据我有此权利、或自认为有此权利而对某物提出要求。
我侵害的是作为权利的权利。
这样的判断属于那些被称为无限的判断。
无限判断不仅从谓词中否定特殊者，而且也否定普遍者；例如：「这个炉子不是鲸鱼」，或者「它不是记忆」。
因为谓词的规定者不仅被否定，其普遍者也被否定，所以主体就一无所余。
这类判断因此是悖理的，但毕竟是对的。
同样，对作为权利的权利的侵害是一件可能的事，并且也确实发生，但它是一件悖理的、自相矛盾的事。
第一类的情形属于民法，第二类的属于刑法。
第一个又叫民事法，第二个叫刑事法。

en: In the first case a mere setting-apart of the grounds of right is necessary, by which it becomes apparent to whom the disputed particular right belongs.
But for this assessment of the views of the two parties a third person is necessary, who is free from their interest in possessing the thing, in order to look simply at right purely as such.
zh: 在第一种情形中，只需把权利根据加以区分就够了，由此可以明见那有争议的特殊权利归属于谁。
不过，为了评判双方的观点，还需要一个第三者，他不受他们占有该物这一利益的牵累，以便纯然就权利本身加以观照。

en: Explanation.
Thus in the first case civil litigation takes place.
In such a case the right of another is claimed, but on the ground of a right.
Both disputing parties agree in this, that they acknowledge right as right.
Only he who has right is to come into possession, and not he who has influence or power and greater merit.
The parties differ from one another only with respect to the subsumption of the particular or of the universal.

It follows from this, accordingly, that no personal insult takes place between the judge and the two parties, insofar as the one is not satisfied with his verdict, nor on the part of the judge against the party to whom he denies right.
Since therefore no attack on what is personal takes place here, it follows that the party which has unjustly attacked the property of another is not punished.
zh: 诠释。
所以在第一种情形中，发生的是民事诉讼。
在这样的场合中，某人的权利被提出要求，但这是凭某种权利根据。
双方当事人于此一致同意：他们把权利承认为权利。
只有有权利的人才应当取得占有，而不是那个有影响力或强力、有更大功绩的人。
双方当事人彼此的分歧，仅在于把特殊者还是把普遍者归摄。
由此可以推出：法官与双方当事人之间不发生人身侮辱，无论是当事人一方对其判决不满意，还是法官对被其否定了权利的那一方。
既然这里没有对人格性的攻击，那么由此可知，那不正当地侵害了他人财产的一方不会受到处罚。

en: The other case, on the contrary, concerns the violation of my personal external freedom, of my body and life, or also of my property as such, through acts of violence.
zh: 相反，第二种情形涉及的是以暴力行为侵害我作为人的外在自由、我的身体和生命，或者也包括我的财产。

en: Explanation.
Among these belongs firstly the wrongful deprivation of my freedom by imprisonment or slavery.
It is a deprivation of the natural external freedom, of not being able to go where one will, and the like. Further, a violation of body and life also belongs here.
The latter is far more significant than the deprivation of my property.
Although life and body are something external, like property, my personality is nevertheless violated in them, because my immediate self-feeling is in my body itself.
zh: 诠释。
其中首先是以监禁或奴役对我的自由所作的不合于法的剥夺。
这就是对自然的、外在的自由——即不能随自己的意愿前往某处——的剥夺，等等。此外，对身体和生命的侵害也属于这里。
后者比对我财产的剥夺重要得多。
虽然生命和身体像财产一样是某种外在的东西，但其中被侵害的还是我的人格性，因为我的直接自我感觉就在我的身体本身之中。

en: The coercion established by such an action must not only be lifted, i.e. the inner nullity of such an action must not only be represented negatively, but the retaliation must also positively occur.
(The form of rationality as such, universality or equality, must be asserted against them.)
For insofar as the actor is a rational being, it lies in his action that it be something universal.
If you rob another, you rob yourself!
If you kill someone, you kill everyone and yourself!
The action is a law which you establish and which you have precisely acknowledged in and for itself through your acting.
The actor may therefore be subsumed under the same mode of action which he has established, and insofar so the equality violated by him is restored: ius talionis.
zh: 由这样一个行为所设置的强制，不仅必须加以扬弃，即这样行为的内在无效性不仅必须从否定方面加以展示，而且报复还必须以正面的方式发生。
（必须针对这些行为主张理性的一般形式，即普遍性或等同。）
因为行动者是一个有理性的存在者，所以他的行为所要求的就是：它应当是某种普遍的东西。
你若抢夺他人，便是抢夺你自己！
你若杀死某人，你便杀死了所有人和你自己！
这一行为就是一部法律：你树立了它，并且你恰恰通过自己的行为自在自为地承认了它。
因此，行动者可以被归摄于他自己所树立的同一种行为方式之下；就这一点而言，那被他所侵害的等同得以恢复：ius talionis。

en: Explanation.
Retaliation rests in general on the rational nature of the one who acts unjustly, or it consists in this, that the unjust must turn itself into right.
The unjust action is indeed a single, irrational action.
But since it is carried out by a rational being, it is, indeed not with respect to its content but with respect to its form, something rational and universal.
Further, it is to be considered as a principle or law.
But as such it at the same time holds only for the actor, because only he acknowledges it through his action, not the others.
He himself therefore essentially belongs under this principle or this law, which must be carried out upon him.
The injustice which he has committed, carried out upon him, is right, because through this second action, which he has acknowledged, a restoration of equality is established.
This is merely formal right.
zh: 诠释。
报复总归以不法行为者的理性的本性为根据，或者说，报复在于：不法必须转化成为法。
不法行为固然是一个个别的、无理性的行为。
但因为它是由一个有理性的存在者实施的，所以它虽然就其内容而言并非如此、但就其形式而言却是一件合乎理性而普遍的东西。
此外，它还应当被看作一条原则或一项法律。
但作为这样的原则或法律，它同时只对行动者有效，因为只有他通过自己的行为承认它，其他人并不承认。
所以他本人本质上就属于这条原则或这项法律之下，这项法律必须在他身上被执行。
他所施行的那种不义，在他身上被执行出来，就是法的，因为通过他所承认的这一第二重行为，等同便得到了恢复。
这只是形式的权利。

en: Retaliation, however, is not to be exercised by the individual who has been offended or by his relatives, because with them the general consideration of right is at the same time bound up with the contingency of passion.
It must be the action of a third person holding power, who merely asserts and carries out the universal.
Insofar it is punishment.
zh: 然而，报复不应由受侵害的个人或其亲属来施行，因为在它们那里，对权利的一般顾及同时又与情欲的偶然性纠缠在一起。
它必须是握有权力的第三方所采取的行动，这位第三方只是主张并实行那普遍者。
就此而言，它就是刑罚。

en: Explanation.
Revenge and punishment differ from one another in that revenge is a retaliation insofar as it is exercised by the offended party, but punishment insofar as it is exercised by the judge.
Retaliation must therefore be exercised as punishment, because in revenge passion has an influence and right is thereby clouded.
Further, revenge does not have the form of right but that of arbitrariness, in that the offended party always acts from feeling or from a subjective motive.
For that reason right, when exercised as revenge, is again a new insult; it is only experienced as an individual action, and so it propagates itself unreconciled into infinity.
zh: 诠释。
复仇与刑罚彼此区别在于：复仇在被侵害的一方施行时是一种报复，而刑罚则是在由法官施行时才如此。
因此，报复必须作为刑罚来施行，因为在复仇中情欲具有影响，权利由此变得浑浊。
此外，复仇并不具有法的形式，而具有任意的形式，因为受侵害的一方总是出于感觉或主观的动力而行动。
因此，法一旦作为复仇来施行，就又成了一项新的侵害；它只被感受为一个别的行为，于是就这样未经和解地把自己延续到无限。

en: The concept of right, as the power which holds force and is independent of the motives of individuality, has reality only in the state society.
zh: 权利概念，作为握有强力并且独立于个别性之动力的那种威力，只有在国家社会里才具有现实性。

en: The family is the natural society whose members are bound together by love, trust, and natural obedience (piety).
zh: 家庭是自然的社会，其成员由爱、信任和自然的服从（孝敬）联结在一起。

en: Explanation.

The family is a natural society, firstly, because someone belongs to a family not through his will but through nature as a member, and secondly, because the relations and the behavior of the members toward one another rest not so much on deliberation and resolve as on feeling and impulse.
The relations are necessary and rational, but the form of conscious insight is lacking.
It is more instinct.
The love of the family members rests on this, that my I forms a unity with the other single I.
They do not regard themselves toward one another as individuals.
The family is an organic whole.
The parts are properly not parts but members, which have their substance only in the whole and to which, separated from the whole, independence is lacking.
The trust which the family members have toward one another consists in this, that each one has not an interest for himself but altogether for the whole.
The natural obedience within the family rests on this, that in this whole there is only one will, namely that which belongs to the head of the household.
Insofar the family makes up only one person.
(Nation.)
zh: 诠释。
家庭是自然的社会：第一，因为一个人不是出于自己的意志、而是出于自然作为成员属于一个家庭；第二，因为各成员彼此之间的关系和行为，其根据与其说是深思和决断，不如说是感觉和冲动。
这些关系是必然的和合乎理性的，但缺少有意识的洞察这一形式。
它更多的是本能。
家庭成员之间的爱建立在这一点上：我的自我与另一个个别的自我构成一个统一。
他们彼此并不把自己看作个别者。
家庭是一个有机的整体。
这些部分其实不是部分，而是成员：它们只在整体中才有其实体，而一旦同整体分离，它们就缺少独立自主性。
家庭成员彼此之间的信任在于：每一个人所关心的不是自己的利益，而根本上说是整体的利益。
家庭内部的自然服从建立在这一点上：在这个整体中只有一个意志，即归于家长的那个意志。
就此而言，家庭只构成一个人格。
（民族。）

en: The state is the society of men under legal relations, in which they count for one another not on account of a particular natural relation, according to natural inclinations and feelings, but as persons, and this personality of each is asserted in a mediated way.
When a family has expanded into a nation and the state coincides in one with the nation, this is a great piece of luck.
zh: 国家是人们在法的关系之下的社会；在其中，人们彼此之所以相待，不是因为某种特殊的自然关系、依照自然的倾向和感觉，而是作为人格；并且每个人格的这一人格性都以间接的方式得到主张。
当一个家族扩展为一个民族、而国家与民族合而为一时，这就是一件大幸运。

en: Explanation.
A people hangs together through language, customs, habit, and education.
This connection, however, does not yet constitute a state.

Furthermore, the morality, religion, prosperity, and wealth of all its citizens are indeed very important for the state, and it must also take care to promote these circumstances; but they do not constitute for it the immediate purpose, but right does.
zh: 诠释。
一个民族靠语言、习俗、习惯和教养联结在一起。
但这种联系还不构成一个国家。
此外，其全体公民的道德、宗教、兴旺和财富对国家固然非常重要，国家也应当关注以促成这些情形；但构成国家的直接目的并不是它们，而是法。

en: The state of nature is the condition of rudeness, force, and injustice.
Men must pass out of such a state into the state society, because only in it does the legal relation have reality.
zh: 自然状态是粗暴、强力与不正义的状态。
人们必须从这样的状态进入国家社会，因为法的关系只有在国家社会中才具有现实性。

en: Explanation.
The state of nature is often accustomed to be described as a perfect condition of man, both with respect to happiness and with respect to moral goodness.
For a first thing it is to be noted that innocence as such has no moral value, insofar as it is ignorance of evil and rests on the lack of needs under which evil can occur.
Secondly, this condition is rather a condition of force and of injustice, precisely because men in it regard themselves according to nature.
According to this, however, they are unequal, both with regard to physical powers and to mental capacities, and they make their difference tell against one another through force and cunning.
Reason is indeed also present in the state of nature, but what is natural is what rules.
Men must therefore pass out of it into a condition in which rational will is what rules.
zh: 诠释。
自然状态常被描绘为人的一种完满状态，无论从至福来说还是从伦理的善来说。
首先应当指出：天真本身并没有道德的价值，因为它是对恶的无知，并且建立在各种需求尚不具备的基础上，而正是在这些需求之下恶才可能发生。
其次，这个状态毋宁说是强力与不正义的状态，恰恰因为人们在其中按自然来相互看待。
但按自然来看，他们彼此不等同，无论就身体的力量还是就精神的禀赋而言，并且他们以强力与机巧相互炫示其差别。
理性在自然状态中固然也存在，但起支配作用的是自然的东西。
因此人们必须从它转入这样一个状态：在其中起支配作用的是有理性的意志。

en: The law is the abstract expression of the general will which is in and for itself.
zh: 法律是自在自为的那个普遍意志的抽象表达。

en: Explanation.
The law is the general will insofar as it is according to reason.
In this it is not necessary that each individual should have known or found this will merely by himself.
Nor is it necessary that each individual should have declared his will and that a general result was then drawn from it.

For that reason, in actual history it did not happen either that every single citizen of a people proposed a law and then came to an agreement about the law with the others through common deliberation.
The law contains the necessity of the legal relations toward one another.
The legislators have not given arbitrary enactments.
These are not determinations of their particular whim, but they have recognized through their profound spirit what the truth and the essence of a legal relation is.
zh: 诠释。
法律是普遍意志，只要它是合乎理性的。
在这里，并不必要求每一个个人仅凭自己就知道或找到这个意志。
同样，也不必要求每一个个人都表达过自己的意志，然后由此得出一个普遍的结果。
因此，在实际的历史中事情也并不是这样发生的：并非每一个民族的每一个公民都提出过一项法律，然后通过与他人共同商议就法律达成一致。
法律包含着法的关系彼此之间的必然性。
立法者所给出的并不是任意的规定。
这些并不是出于他们特别的任性而作的规定，而是他们以其深沉的精神认识到，一个法的关系的真理与本质是什么。

en: The government is the individuality of the will which is in and for itself.
It is the power which gives the laws and handles or executes them.
zh: 政府是自在自为的那个意志的个别性。
它是那种给予法律并加以运用或执行的力量。

en: Explanation.
The state has laws.
These are therefore the will in its universal abstract essence, which as such is inert, - as principles and maxims express or contain only as yet the universal of willing, not yet an actual willing.
Only the government is the active and realizing will corresponding to this universal.
The law does indeed persist as custom, as habit, but the government is the conscious power of the unconscious habit.
zh: 诠释。
国家有法律。
这些法律因而就是意志处在其普遍的抽象本质之中的形态，而这个本质作为这样的形态是不活动的——正如原则和准则所表达或包含的还只是意愿的普遍者，而不是一种现实的意愿。
与这一普遍者相应的，只有政府是那个能动的、使其现实化的意志。
法律固然作为习俗、作为习惯而存在，但政府是那无意识的习惯的有意识的威力。

en: The general state power contains various particular powers subsumed under it: 1. the legislative as such; 2. the administrative and financial, which create the means for the realization of freedom; 3. the (independent) judicial and police; 4. the military and the power to wage war and conclude peace.
zh: 一般国家权力包含着归摄于其下的各种特殊强力：1. 立法权本身；2. 行政权与财政权，它们为自由的现实化造就手段；3. （独立的）司法权与警察权；4. 军事权以及进行战争和缔结和平的权力。

en: Explanation.

The kind of constitution depends primarily on whether these particular powers are exercised immediately by the center of the government; further, whether several of them are combined in one authority or, on the contrary, whether they are separate, e.g. whether the prince or regent himself pronounces right immediately or whether separate special courts have been established; further, whether the regent also combines the ecclesiastical power within himself, etc.

It is also important whether in a constitution the supreme center of the government has the financial power in an unrestricted sense in its hands, such that it can both impose and use taxes entirely according to its arbitrariness.
Further, whether several authorities are combined in one, e.g. whether in a single official the judicial and the military power are united.
The kind of a constitution is further determined by whether all citizens, insofar as they are citizens, have a share in the government.
Such a constitution is a democracy.

The degeneration of this is the ochlocracy or the rule of the mob, namely when that part of the people which has no property and is of unjust sentiments keeps the legal citizens away from state affairs by force.

Only with simple, uncorrupted customs and a small extent of the state can a democracy occur and maintain itself. - The aristocracy is the constitution in which only some certain privileged families have the exclusive right to government.
The degeneration of this is the oligarchy, namely when the number of the families which have the right to government is a small number.

Such a condition is dangerous, because in an oligarchy all the particular powers are exercised immediately by a council. - The monarchy is the constitution in which the government remains in the hands of a single individual and is hereditary in one family.

In a hereditary monarchy the disputes and civil wars are eliminated which can occur in an elective state at a change of the throne, because the ambition of powerful individuals can form no hope for the throne.

Nor can the monarch exercise the whole governmental power immediately, but he entrusts a part of the exercise of the particular powers to colleges or also to the imperial estates, which in the name of the king, under his supervision and direction, exercise the power entrusted to them according to the laws.
In a monarchy civil freedom is more protected than in other constitutions.
The degeneration of the monarchy is despotism, namely when the regent exercises the government immediately according to his arbitrariness.
It is essential to the monarchy that the government have emphasis and proper force against the private interest of individuals.
But on the other hand the rights of the citizens must also be protected by laws.
A despotic government indeed has the highest power, but in such a constitution the rights of the citizens are sacrificed.

The despot indeed has the greatest power and can use the forces of his realm according to arbitrariness, but this standpoint is also the most dangerous. - The governmental constitution of a people is not merely an external arrangement.
A people can just as well have this as another constitution.
It depends essentially on the character, the customs, the degree of education, the mode of life, and the extent of the people.
zh: 诠释。
宪法的样式主要取决于：这些特殊强力是否由政府的中心直接行使；其次取决于，其中几项是否合并于一个权威之内，抑或彼此分开，例如君主或摄政者本人是否直接宣判权利，抑或另设有专门的法院；其次还取决于，摄政者是否也把教会的权力合并于自身，等等。
同样重要的是：在一宪法中，政府的最高中心是否在无限的意义上把财政权掌握在自己手里，以至它完全依自己的任意既能征税、也能用税。
其次，几项权威是否合并为一，例如在一个官员身上司法权与军事权是否合而为一。
一宪法的样式还取决于：所有公民是否就其作为公民而言都参与政府。
这样的宪法就是民主制。
它的变质是民众统治或群氓的统治，即：当人民中那个没有财产、并且怀有不正当心态的部分，以强力把合法的公民挡在国家事务之外的时候。
只有在淳朴而未腐化的习俗以及国家幅员狭小的条件下，民主制才可能出现并维持自身。——贵族制是这样的宪法：只有某些特定的享有特权的家族对政府拥有排他的权利。
它的变质是寡头制，即：当拥有政府权利的家族数量甚少的时候。
这样的状态之所以危险，是因为在寡头制中一切特殊强力都由一个议事会直接行使。——君主制是这样的宪法：政府留在一个人手中，并且在一个家族中世袭。
在世袭君主制中，选举制国家在王位更迭时可能发生的纷争和公民战争便不复存在，因为有势力者的野心不能对王位抱有任何指望。
君主同样也不能直接行使全部的政府权力；他要把特殊权力之行使的一部分委托给各委员会，或者也委托给帝国等级；这些机构以国王的名义、在他的监督和领导之下，依照法律行使所授予它们的权力。
在君主制中，公民自由比在其他宪法下受到更多的保护。
君主制的变质是专制，即：当摄政者按照自己的任意直接行使政府权力的时候。
君主制的本质在于：政府对于各个人的私人利益具有强调的力量和应有的强力。
但另一方面，公民的权利也必须由法律加以保护。
专制的政府固然拥有最高的强力，但在这样的宪法中，公民的权利是被牺牲掉的。
专制者固然拥有最大的强力，能按自己的任意使用其国家的力量，但这一立场也是最危险的。——一个民族的宪法形式不只是一种外在的设置。
一个民族同样可以有这一种宪法，也可以有另一种宪法。
它根本上取决于该民族的性状、习俗、教养的程度、生活方式和幅员。

en: The citizens as individuals are subjected to the state power and obey it.

Its content and purpose, however, is the realization of the natural, i.e. absolute rights of citizens, who in the state do not renounce them but rather alone attain them there for their enjoyment and their development.
zh: 公民作为个人服从于国家权力，并服从于它。
但它的内容和目的，是公民的自然权利即绝对权利的现实化；公民在国家中并不放弃这些权利，而唯独在国家中才得以享用并展开它们。

en: The state constitution determines, as internal state law, the relation of the particular powers both to the government, their highest union, and to one another, as well as the relation of the citizens to it or their share in it.
zh: 国家宪法作为内在的国家法，既确定特殊强力同政府（它们最高的统一）之间的关系，也确定它们彼此之间的关系，并且确定公民同它的关系或公民在其中的份额。

en: The external state law concerns the relation of independent peoples to one another through their governments and rests primarily on particular treaties, - law of nations
zh: 外在的国家法涉及各个独立民族通过其政府彼此之间的关系，并主要建立在各项特殊条约之上——即万国法

en: Explanation.
The states find themselves toward one another more in a natural than in a legal relation.
There is therefore a perpetual strife among them, such that they conclude treaties with one another and thereby set themselves in a legal relation toward one another.
On the other hand, however, they are entirely independent of one another.
Right is therefore not actual between them.
They can therefore arbitrarily break the treaties and must always be in a certain distrust toward one another about them.
As natural beings they behave toward one another according to force, in that they must preserve themselves in their right, must create right for themselves, and thus fall into war with one another.
zh: 诠释。
各国彼此之间与其说处于法的关系，不如说更多处于自然的关系。
因此它们之间存在着持久的纷争，以致它们彼此缔结条约，从而把彼此置于法的关系之中。
但另一方面，它们又完全独立，互不依赖。
所以权利在它们之间并不现实。
因此它们可以任意撕毁条约，并且在这方面必定彼此保持着某种不信任。
作为自然存在物，它们彼此按强力行事，即它们必须在自己的权利中保全自己、必须为自己创造权利，因而就这样彼此陷入战争。

91.en: Second Part: Doctrine of Duty or Morality
91.zh: 第二部分 义务论或道德学说

en: What can be demanded according to right is a liability.
Duty, however, is something insofar as it is to be observed for moral reasons.
zh: 按权利所能要求的是一种责任。
但义务是某种就其出于道德理由而应予遵守的东西。

en: Explanation.
The word duty is frequently used of legal relations.

One determined the legal duties to be perfect and the moral ones imperfect, because the former must occur altogether and have an external necessity, whereas the moral duties rest on a subjective will.

One could, however, just as well reverse the determination, because legal duty as such demands only an external necessity, in which the disposition may be lacking; indeed I can even have a bad intention in it.
For the moral disposition, on the contrary, both are required, both the right action with respect to its content and, with respect to its form, the subjective of the disposition.
zh: 诠释。
「义务」一词常常被用于法的关系。
人们曾把法权义务规定为完满的，把道德的义务规定为不完满的，因为前者总之必须发生、并具有外在的必然性，而道德的义务则建立在主观的意志之上。
但人们同样可以把这个规定倒过来，因为法权义务作为这样的义务只要求一种外在的必然性，其中心态可以缺失；甚至我还可以怀着恶劣的意图去做。
相反，对道德的心态来说两者都是必需的：就内容而言行为要正确，就形式而言则要有心态的主观性。

en: Right leaves the disposition free altogether.
Morality, on the contrary, essentially concerns the disposition and demands that the action occur out of respect for duty.
Thus legal conduct is also moral insofar as it has respect for right as its motive.
zh: 权利总的来说让心态自由。
相反，道德本质上关涉心态，并要求行为出于对义务的敬重而发生。
所以，法上的行为只要以对权利的敬重为动机，也同样是道德的。

en: The disposition is the subjective side of the moral action or its form.
No content is as yet present in it, which, like actual acting, is equally essential.
zh: 心态是道德行为的主观方面，或者说，是它的形式。
其中还没有任何内容；而这种内容如同现实的行动一样，是同样本质性的。

en: Explanation.
With legal conduct the moral is essentially also to be connected.
But it may also be the case that the disposition of right is not connected with legal conduct, and indeed that an unmoral disposition is present in it.
The legal action is at the same time also moral insofar as it occurs out of respect for the law.

Legal acting - and at the same time along with the moral disposition - is to be pursued in the first instance, and only then can moral acting as such enter, in which there is no legal command (no legal liability).
Men like to act merely morally or nobly, and often rather give away than fulfil their legal liabilities.
For in the noble action they give themselves the consciousness of their particular perfection, whereas in legal acting they exercise the perfectly universal, which is equal for them with everyone.
zh: 诠释。
在法的行为上，实质上也应当连带着道德。
但也可能出现这样的情况：法的行为并没有同对权利的心态相联结，甚至其中还带着一种不合道德的心态。
法的行为只要是出于对法律的敬重而发生的，就同时也是道德的。
法的行动——同时连同道德的心态——总之总是首先要加以遵循的；只有这样，作为这样的道德行动才可能出现，其中并没有法的命令（没有法权责任）。
人们喜欢仅仅凭道德或高尚行事，而且常常宁可赠与，也不愿履行他们的法权责任。
因为在高贵的行动中，他们使自己获得对其特殊完满性的意识；而在法的行动中，他们实行的则是完全普遍的东西，那是他们与所有人所共有的。

en: Everything actual contains two sides, the true concept and the reality of this concept; e.g. the concept of the state is the guarantee and the realization of right.
To the reality belong now the particular arrangement of the constitution, the relation of the individual powers, etc.
To the actual man there also belongs, namely according to his practical side, the concept and the reality of the concept.
To the former belongs pure personality or abstract freedom, to the latter the particular determinacy of determinate being and determinate being itself.
Although there is contained in the latter something more than in the concept, yet at the same time it must be conform to the concept and determined through it.
The pure concept of practical determinate being, the I, is the object of right.
zh: 一切现实的东西都包含两个侧面：真正的概念以及这一概念的实在性；例如，国家的概念就是权利的保障和现实化。
属于实在性的，是宪法的特殊设置、各项强力之间的关系等等。
属于现实的人、并且是就其实践的方面而言的，同样还有概念以及概念的实在性。
属于前者的，是纯粹的人格性或抽象的自由；属于后者的，是定在的特殊规定以及定在本身。
后者之中固然比概念所含的要多，但同时它必须符合于概念、并通过概念而得到规定。
实践的定在的纯粹概念，即自我，是权利的对象。

en: The moral mode of action refers to man not as abstract person but to him according to the general and necessary determinations of his particular determinate being.

It is therefore not merely prohibitive, as the legal command actually is, which only commands that the freedom of the other be left untouched, but commands that a positive be shown to the other as well.
The precepts of morality have to do with individual actuality.
zh: 道德的行为方式所指向的，不是作为抽象人格的人，而是按照其特殊定在的普遍而必然的规定的人。
因此它并不只是禁止性的——法的命令其实才是禁止性的，它只命令不去触动他人的自由——而且还命令向他人做出积极的行为。
道德的训诫指向的是个别现实性。

en: The drive of man toward his particular determinate being, as morality regards it, has to do with the correspondence of the external as such with his inner determinations, with pleasure and happiness.
zh: 按照道德的看法，人朝向其特殊定在的冲动，总体上着眼于外在者与其内在规定之间的相合，着眼于快乐和至福。

en: Explanation.
Man has drives, i.e. he has inner determinations in his nature or according to that side according to which he is an actual being at all.
These determinations are therefore something deficient insofar as they are only something internal.
They are drives insofar as they aim at lifting this deficiency, i.e. they demand their realization, the correspondence of the external with the internal.
This correspondence is the pleasure.
Therefore a reflection as a comparison between the internal and the external precedes it, whether this derive from me or from fortune.
The pleasure can now arise from the most manifold sources.
It does not depend on the content but concerns only the form, or it is the feeling of something merely formal, namely of the indicated correspondence.
The doctrine which has the pleasure, or rather the happiness, as its purpose has been called eudaimonism.
But in it it is undetermined in what one is to seek the pleasure or the happiness.
There can therefore be an entirely raw, crude eudaimonism, but just as well a better one; namely good as well as bad actions can ground themselves on this principle.
zh: 诠释。
人具有冲动，也就是说，他在他的本性中具有内在的规定，或者说，按照他总是一个现实存在者这一侧面而具有内在的规定。
这些规定因此是有缺陷的，就它们仅仅是一种内在的东西而言。
它们是冲动，就它们旨在扬弃这一缺陷而言，也就是说，它们要求自己的现实化，即要求外在者与内在者的相合。
这一相合就是快乐。
因此，在它之前先有一种反思，即内在者与外在者之间的比较，无论这是出自我还是出自幸运。
快乐于是可以从最各种各样的来源产生。
它并不取决于内容，而只涉及形式；或者说，它是某种纯粹形式的东西的感觉，即上述相合的感觉。
以快乐、或者更确切地说以至福为目的之学说，被称为幸福主义。
但在这学说中，人们应当在何处寻求快乐或至福，是不确定的。
因此可能存在一种完全粗野、粗陋的幸福主义，但同样也可能有一种更好的；即善的行为和恶的行为同样可以建立在这一原则之上。

en: This correspondence as pleasure is a subjective feeling and something contingent, which can attach itself to this or that drive and its object, and in which I am an end only as a natural being and only as an individual.
zh: 这一相合作为快乐，是一种主观的感觉和某种偶然的东西；它可以系于这样或那样的冲动及其对象，而在其中，我只有在作为自然存在者、并且只有作为个别者时才是目的。

en: Explanation.
The pleasure is something subjective and refers merely to me as a particular individual.
What is objective, universal, intelligible is not in it.
It is therefore no standard and no rule by which a thing is judged or adjudged.
When I say that it pleases me too, or appeal to my pleasure, I merely express that the thing holds for me in such and such a way, and have thereby lifted the intelligible relation with others.
It is contingent with respect to its content because it can attach itself to this or that object, and since it does not depend on the content, it is something formal.
According to its external determinate being as well, the pleasure is contingent, [because it is contingent] to find the circumstances.
The means which I need for this are something external and do not depend on me.
Secondly, the determinate being which I have brought about through the means must, insofar as it is to please me, become mine, come to me.
But this is the contingent.
The consequences of what I do therefore do not return to me.

I do not necessarily have the enjoyment of them. - The pleasure thus arises from two kinds of circumstances: firstly from a determinate being which one has to find, which depends entirely on fortune; and secondly from one which I myself bring forth.

This determinate being indeed depends on my will as the effect of my deed, but only the action as such belongs to me; the success, on the contrary, need not necessarily come back to me, and consequently neither the enjoyment of the action.
In such an action as that of Decius Mus for his fatherland, it lies that the effect of it should not return to him as enjoyment.
In short, the consequences are not to be made into the principle of the action.
The consequences of an action are contingent because they are an external determinate being which depends on other circumstances or can be lifted.
zh: 诠释。
快乐是某种主观的东西，它仅仅指向作为个别者的我。
其中并没有客观的、普遍的和可理解的东西。
所以它不是一种尺度，也不是一种据以评判或裁判某物的规则。
当我说它同样合我的意、或者我援引我的快乐时，我所说的不过只是：这件事物对我而言具有这样的效力；这样我就扬弃了与他人之间可理解的关系。
就其内容而言它是偶然的，因为它可以系于这样或那样的对象；而既然它并不取决于内容，它就是某种形式的东西。
就其外在的定在而言，快乐同样是偶然的，[因为]偶然地发现这些情境。
我为此需要的手段是某种外在的东西，并且不取决于我。
其次，我通过这些手段所造成的定在，就其要使我快乐而言，必须成为我的、来到我这里。
但这就是偶然的东西。
因此，我所做的事情的后果并不返回于我。
我并不必然享有它们的享受。——所以快乐产生于两种情形：第一，产生于一种必须去发现的定在，这全然取决于幸运；第二，产生于我自己造成的那种定在。
这一定在固然作为我行为的效果而取决于我的意志，但只有行动本身才属于我；相反，其成功却不必必然回到我这里，因而行动的享受也不必必然回到我这里。
在像 Decius Mus 为其祖国所采取的那种行为里，所包含的正是：其效果不应当作为享受回到他身上。
总之，不应当把后果当作行为的原则。
一个行为的后果是偶然的，因为它们是一种外在的定在，取决于其他情境，或者可以被扬弃。

en: The pleasure is a secondary thing, something accompanying the deed.
Insofar as the substantial is realized, the pleasure is added in that one recognizes in the work one’s subjective as well.
He who pursues pleasure seeks only himself according to his accidentality.
He who is occupied with great works and interests strives only to bring the thing in itself to actuality.
He is directed toward the substantial, does not remember himself in it, forgets himself in the thing.
Men of great interests and labors are commonly pitied by the people for having little pleasure, i.e. for living only in the thing and not in their accidentality.
zh: 快乐是次要的东西，是伴随着行为的东西。
在实体性的东西得以现实化之处，快乐就附加上来，因为人们在作品中也认出了自己的主观性。
追逐快乐的人，只是在按自己的偶性寻求自己。
忙于伟大作品和重大事务的人，只是力图把事情本身带进现实性。
他指向实体性的东西，不在其中记起自己，而是在事情中忘掉了自己。
有重大事务与劳作的人常被民众惋惜，说他们很少有快乐；也就是说，他们只生活在事情之中，而不出在他们自己的偶性之中。

en: Reason lifts the indeterminacy which the agreeable feeling has with regard to objects, purges the content of the drives of the subjective and the contingent, and teaches with respect to the content to know the universal and the essential of the desirable, but with respect to the form or the disposition the objective or the acting for the sake of the thing itself.
zh: 理性扬弃愉快的感觉在看待对象时所具有的不定性，把冲动的内容从主观和偶然之中净化出来；并且就内容方面教会人认识值得欲求之物的普遍者与本质者，就形式或心态方面则教会人认识客观的东西，或者为事情本身而行动。

en: Explanation.
First the understanding or the reflection goes beyond the immediate pleasure, but does not change the purpose or the principle.

Insofar it goes beyond only the individual pleasure, it compares the drives with one another and can therefore prefer the one to the other. - Insofar as it is directed not to the pleasure as an individual thing but to the pleasure in the whole, it intends happiness.
This reflection still stays within the subjective principle and still has the pleasure as its purpose, but only the greater, more manifold one.

Insofar as it makes distinctions in pleasure and seeks the agreeable on all the different sides as such, it refines the raw, wild, and merely animal nature of pleasure and moderates the customs and the dispositions as such.

Insofar, therefore, the understanding occupies itself with the means of satisfying needs as such, it thereby facilitates this satisfaction and thereby preserves the possibility of devoting itself to higher purposes. - On the other hand, this refinement of pleasures makes man more soft.

Insofar as he employs his powers on so manifold objects and forms for himself so manifold purposes, which become ever smaller through the distinguishing of their different sides, his power is weakened as such for directing himself with his whole spirit toward the essential.
If man makes pleasure his purpose, he lifts through this reflection the drive to go beyond it and to do something higher.
zh: 诠释。
起初，知性或反思越出直接的东西这种快乐，但它并不改变目的或原则。
就此而言，它只是越出个别的东西这种快乐，把各个冲动彼此比较，因而可以厚此薄彼。——当它指向的不是个别者的快乐而是整体中的快乐时，它所意欲的就是至福。
这种反思仍然停留在主观的原则之内，仍以快乐为目的，只不过是那更大的、更多样的快乐。
当它在快乐中造成差别、总体上在一切不同侧面寻求愉快之物时，它就使快乐的粗野、放肆和纯然兽性的成分变得精细，并总体上缓和了习俗与心态。
因此，就知性忙于谋求满足各种需求的手段而言，它借此使这种满足变得容易，并借此保住了献身于更高目的之可能。——另一方面，这种对快乐的精细化使人变得柔弱。
当他把自己的力量用在如此多样的对象上、为自己设立如此多样的目的，而这些目的又由于其不同侧面被区分而越来越小的时候，他的力量总体上就被削弱了，不再能以全部精神指向本质的东西。
当人把快乐当作目的时，他就通过这种反思扬弃了越出它、去做某种更高之事的冲动。

en: The pleasure is undetermined with respect to its content because it can occur with all objects.
With respect to it, therefore, no objective distinction can be made, only a quantitative one.
The understanding, calculating the consequences, prefers the greater to the smaller.
zh: 就其内容而言快乐是不定的，因为它可以在一切对象上发生。
因此，就它而言不能作出客观的差别，只能作出量的差别。
知性在计算后果时，把较大者置于较小者之上。

en: Reason, on the contrary, makes a qualitative distinction, i.e. a distinction with respect to the content.
It prefers the worthy object of pleasure to the unworthy one.
It therefore goes into a comparison of the nature of the objects.
Insofar it no longer considers the subjective as such, namely the agreeable feeling, but the objective.
It therefore teaches what objects man is to desire for their own sake.

In the case of man, in whose general nature such infinitely manifold sources of pleasure are open, the direction toward the agreeable is deceptive as such, and he lets himself easily be distracted by this manifoldness, i.e. diverted from a purpose which he should make into his determination.
zh: 相反，理性作出质的差别，即就内容而言的差别。
它把值得的快乐对象置于不值得的对象之上。
所以它进而从事于对对象本性的比较。
就此而言，它所考察的不再是主观的东西，即那种愉快的感觉，而是客观的东西。
所以它教会人：人应当为哪些对象自身而欲求它们。
就人而言，由于其普遍的本性向他开放着如此无限多样的快乐之源，总体上朝向愉快之物的方向是骗人的；而且他很容易被这种多样性弄得心神分散，也就是被引离那个他本应使之成为自己规定的目的。

en: The drive of the agreeable can agree with reason, i.e. that both have the same content, that reason legitimates the content. - With respect to the form, the drive acts for the sake of the subjective feeling or has the agreeable of the subject as its purpose.
In action for the sake of a universal object, the object itself is the purpose.
The drive of the agreeable, on the contrary, is always selfish.
zh: 愉快之物的冲动可以与理性一致，也就是说，两者具有同一的内容，即理性使这一内容正当。——就形式而言，这种冲动是为了主观的感觉而行动，或者以主体的愉快之物为目的。
在为着一个普遍对象而行动时，对象本身就是目的。
相反，愉快之物的冲动总是利己的。

en: The drives and inclinations are 1. considered in themselves neither good nor evil, i.e. man has them immediately as a natural being.
Good and evil are moral determinations and belong to the will.
The good is that which corresponds to reason.
Drives and inclinations, however, cannot be considered without relation to the will.
This relation is not contingent and man is no indifferent double being.
zh: 冲动和倾向 1. 就自在的而言既非善也非恶，也就是说，人作为自然存在者直接地具有它们。
善与恶是道德的规定，属于意志。
善是与理性相应的东西。
但冲动和倾向不能不联系于意志来考察。
这一关系不是偶然的，人也不是一个漠然无干的双重存在物。

en: Explanation.
Morality has man in his particularity as its object.
This seems at first to contain only a multiplicity of the diverse, the unlike which distinguishes men from one another.
That by which men are distinguished from one another is the contingent, that which depends on nature and external circumstances.
But something universal is at the same time contained in the particular.
The particularity of man consists in the relation to others.
In this relation there are now also essential and necessary determinations.
These constitute the content of duty.
zh: 诠释。
道德以人的特殊性为对象。
这起初似乎只包含着多样事物的一堆，即把人彼此区分开来的那种不同。
人们彼此被区分开的东西，乃是偶然的，即依赖于自然和外在情境的东西。
但在特殊者之中同时也包含着某种普遍的东西。
人的特殊性在于他与其他人的关系之中。
在这一关系中现在也有本质性的和必然的规定。
这些构成义务的内容。

en: Man has 1. the essential determination to be an individual, 2. he belongs to a natural whole, the family, 3. he is a member of the state, 4. he stands in relation to other men as such. - The duties therefore divide into four kinds: 1. duties toward himself, 2. toward the family, 3. toward the state, and 4. toward other men as such.
zh: 人 1. 有成为一个个别者的本质规定，2. 属于一个自然的整体，即家庭，3. 是国家的成员，4. 总而言之与其他的人处于关系之中。——所以义务分为四类：1. 对自己的义务，2. 对家庭的义务，3. 对国家的义务，4. 总而言之对其他人的义务。
